Report.listDescription: Official results for the students in your classes.
Report.listPanelDescription: {count, plural, =0 {No results yet} one {# result} other {# results}}
Report.listEmptyDescription: A report appears here once one of your students completes an official sitting and scoring finishes.
Report.listGoneTitle: This report list is no longer available

Report.reportGoneTitle: This report is no longer available
Report.reportGoneDescription: It may have been removed, or the link may be out of date.
Report.displayLabelPendingDescription: The display label appears once scoring completes for this sitting.
Report.displayLabelNotApplicable: No display label for this skill
Report.displayLabelNotApplicableDescription: The label ladder is defined for reading and listening only. Speaking, writing and the placement summary carry none — by design, not as a missing value.
Report.displayLabelSource: Derived from the active crosswalk for this skill. No cut score and no cross-skill composite is used.
Report.provisionalFieldTest: This sitting included field-test items. Their parameters are not calibrated yet, so this result is provisional and may change.
Report.confidenceLowNote: Scoring settled on this attribute pattern with a low posterior probability. Read the attribute detail before acting on the label.
Report.crosswalkSource: ACARA phase, CEFR band and readiness are lookups the active crosswalk carries on this result. No cut score and no cross-skill composite is used.
Report.attributesDescription: One bar per modelled attribute. The bar is the mastery probability; the band beside it is the display status this result was published with.
Report.attributesNotDerivedDescription: Per-attribute evidence appears once scoring completes for this sitting.
Report.attributesNotApplicable: No attribute ladder for this skill
Report.attributesNotApplicableDescription: The attribute ladder is defined for reading and listening only. Speaking, writing and the placement summary carry none — by design, not as a missing value.
Report.attributeNotAssessedNote: No items were administered for this attribute in this sitting.
Report.evidenceSummaryAssessed: {assessed} of {total} attributes assessed; evidence ranges from {min} to {max} items per attribute.
Report.evidenceSummaryNoneAssessed: None of the {total} attributes was administered in this sitting.
Report.confidenceIntervalAbsent: Scoring did not persist a standard error for this result, so precision is shown as evidence volume only — never as an error bar.
Report.attributesSource: Mastery probabilities and their display status come from the scoring engine and the active configuration. No cut score is applied here and no cross-skill composite is used.
Report.supplementaryDescription: Band accuracies from the supplementary vocabulary tasks. They are reported alongside the model, not inside it: they are not one of the modelled attributes, they do not enter the mastery model, and no cut score is applied to them.

supplementaryBandSource.a2: Proportion correct over the Stage 1 vocabulary tasks in this sitting.
supplementaryBandSource.b1: Proportion correct over the Stage 2 synonym-match strand in this sitting.

Report.supplementaryNotAdministeredNote: No items from this band were served in this sitting, so there is no accuracy to report. This is an absence, not a zero.
Report.supplementaryQualifierLink: {count, plural, one {Label qualifier on this result: {qualifiers}.} other {Label qualifiers on this result: {qualifiers}.}} A qualifier is derived from the modelled attributes, never from these bands — read the two together.
Report.supplementarySource: Band accuracies are proportions correct over the vocabulary items served in this sitting. They sit outside the mastery model, carry no cut score and enter no composite.
Report.supplementaryPendingDescription: The vocabulary strand appears once scoring writes the band accuracies for this sitting.
Report.supplementaryNotApplicable: No vocabulary strand for this skill
Report.supplementaryNotApplicableDescription: The supplementary vocabulary strand is administered with reading and listening only. Speaking, writing and the placement summary carry none — by design, not as a missing value.
Report.observationsDescription: Generated from the attribute contrast on this result. Each sentence restates evidence already on this page — no new measurement, no score, and no recommendation the evidence does not carry.
Report.observationsSource: Observations are derived from the per-attribute mastery statuses, their evidence counts and the supplementary band accuracies on this result. No cut score is applied here and no cross-skill composite is used.
Report.observationsNotDerivedDescription: Observations appear once scoring writes the per-attribute evidence for this sitting.
Report.observationsNotApplicable: No layered attribute ladder for this skill
Report.observationsNotApplicableDescription: The two-layer ladder these observations contrast is defined for reading and listening only. Speaking, writing and the placement summary carry none — by design, not as a missing value.
Report.observationsUnclassified: These attribute codes do not follow the receptive ladder
Report.observationsUnclassifiedDescription: An attribute on this result carries no readable ladder position, so it cannot be placed in the foundation or the comprehension layer. Nothing is guessed here.

observations.noAttributeEvidence: No attribute in this sitting carries evidence, so no contrast can be drawn between the foundation and the comprehension layer.
observations.jaggedProfile: {masteredCount, plural, one {Comprehension attribute {mastered} is} other {Comprehension attributes {mastered} are}} mastered while {gapCount, plural, one {the foundation attribute {gap} is} other {the foundation attributes {gap} are}} not — a profile the receptive hierarchy does not expect. Read {gap} as the bottleneck and treat the comprehension claim with care.
observations.comprehensionNotAssessedWithGap: This sitting administered no comprehension items, so the profile speaks to the foundation layer only, where {gapCount, plural, one {attribute {gap} is} other {attributes {gap} are}} not yet secure.
observations.comprehensionNotAssessedFoundationSecure: Every foundation attribute assessed here ({foundation}) is mastered, and this sitting administered no comprehension items — so there is no comprehension claim to set against it.
observations.foundationBottleneck: {blockedCount, plural, one {Comprehension attribute {blocked} is} other {Comprehension attributes {blocked} are}} not yet mastered, while {gapCount, plural, one {the foundation attribute {gap}, which the receptive model requires first, is} other {the foundation attributes {gap}, which the receptive model requires first, are}} not secure — so the bottleneck sits at {gap}, not in comprehension itself.
observations.foundationSecureComprehensionGap: Every foundation attribute assessed here is mastered, so the gap sits inside comprehension: {gapCount, plural, one {attribute {gap} is} other {attributes {gap} are}} not yet mastered.
observations.allMastered: Every attribute assessed in this sitting is mastered, across both the foundation and the comprehension layer, so this result names no bottleneck.
observations.vocabularyBandMeasured: Modelled vocabulary ({code}) carries the status “{status}” at the A2 band, and the supplementary B1 band — which sits outside the model — was answered at {b1} accuracy in this sitting.
observations.vocabularyBandNotAdministered: Modelled vocabulary ({code}) carries the status “{status}” at the A2 band; no B1-band item was served in this sitting, so there is no above-A2 vocabulary reading to set beside it.
observations.vocabularyNotAssessedBandMeasured: No modelled vocabulary item was administered in this sitting, so the only vocabulary reading here is the supplementary B1 band at {b1} accuracy — an out-of-model indicator, not a mastery claim.
observations.evidenceCaveat: {spread, select, uniform {These statements rest on {assessed} of {total} attributes, each evidenced by {maxItems} items.} other {These statements rest on {assessed} of {total} attributes, evidenced by between {minItems} and {maxItems} items each, so read the thinner ones with more caution.}}{lowConfidence, select, true { Scoring also settled on this attribute pattern with a low posterior probability, so treat every statement above as provisional.} other {}}

Report.effortInvalidNote: Responses in this sitting show signs of rushing, so this result may understate what the student can do. Read it alongside classroom evidence.
Report.errorPatternsDescription: Distractor types this student chose repeatedly, aggregated from the responses in this sitting. They describe how the wrong options were chosen, not how much was scored.
Report.errorPatternsSource: Composed by the diagnostic export from the responses recorded in this sitting. A phrase appears only where the same distractor type was chosen on at least two items of an attribute. Nothing here enters the mastery model or any score.
Report.errorPatternsNoneObserved: No repeated error pattern was observed
Report.errorPatternsNoneObservedDescription: The responses in this sitting were aggregated and no distractor type was chosen often enough on any attribute to name a pattern. This is a measured result, not a missing one.
Report.errorPatternsNotApplicable: No error pattern notes for this result
Report.errorPatternsNotApplicableDescription: Error patterns are aggregated from the receptive item responses of a sitting. Speaking and writing results carry none — by design, not as a missing value.
Report.errorPatternsUnavailable: Error pattern notes could not be loaded
Report.errorPatternsUnavailableDescription: The diagnostic export for this result did not answer. Nothing is shown in its place: an empty list here would claim that no error pattern was observed.

viewModeHint.teacher: The full diagnostic record: the crosswalk lookups, the per-attribute evidence and the response-level notes.

hero.title: A different type of English test.
hero.subtitle: See exactly what each EAL/D student can and can't do, subskill by subskill, in 30 minutes per skill.

problem.title: What if you could see inside their minds?
problem.bodyOne: Every EAL/D student arrives as a blunt number: a placement score, a stanine, a CEFR band. They progress through broad ACARA phases. None of it gives you empirical insight into their actual linguistic profile.
problem.bodyTwo: So what to teach Monday, who to group with whom, whether your lessons are working, whether they're ready for mainstream. All of it comes down to intuition. What if you had psychometric data to support you?

solution.intro: A diagnostic and progress test built for EAL/D classrooms, Years 7–12.
solution.body: SchoolTest measures 4 skills and 27 subskills across reading, listening, speaking and writing. 30 minutes per skill, showing ACARA progression every time you test.
solution.tagline: Assessment stops being a summary and starts being a map.

whatYouGet.title: 30-minute in-class tests. Diagnose, teach, track and predict.
whatYouGet.diagnoseDescription: 27 subskills from a 30-minute test. Six weeks of diagnostic testing, done on day one.
whatYouGet.teachDescription: Export a privacy-safe class set into any AI. Differentiation stops being a Sunday night job.
whatYouGet.trackDescription: Every result on the same ACARA scale. If it worked, it shows up.
whatYouGet.predictDescription: One readiness score across all four domains. Exit calls you can defend.

classroom.quote: Assessment stops being a summary and starts being a map.
classroom.subtext: Years 7–12 · Reading, listening, speaking and writing

proof.badge: Built on 40+ years of psychometric research
proof.scalesLabel: Phases and bands, side by side
proof.durationLabel: Per skill, as often as you need

hero.title: One 30-minute test. <blue>A complete diagnostic profile.</blue>
hero.body: SchoolTest breaks each macroskill into its component subskills, so you see exactly where a learner is and what to teach first.

unpack.title: Six weeks of figuring them out, done in 30 minutes.
unpack.body: A new student arrives with a placement score or a stanine. But what's really going on? SchoolTest gives you the complete subskill profile in a single 30-minute sitting, benchmarked to ACARA phases.
unpack.callout: What this means for you: walk into period two knowing exactly what to teach.

profile.moreSubskills: + 18 more across listening, speaking and writing

sameScore.title:
Same score.

Different abilities.
sameScore.body: Two students arrive with the same broad scores. Are they the same? Not at all. One is strong in grammar but weak in inference; the other is the reverse. Each student has a unique linguistic profile that placement tests don't reveal. Now you see it.
sameScore.callout: What this means for you: two students you'd have taught together, taught properly.

diagnose.quote:
A score is a summary.

A subskill profile is a map.

hero.title: Know when a student is ready for mainstream, <blue>and prove it.</blue>
hero.body: One readiness indicator built from every subskill across all four skills. When you exit a student, you'll know they're ready. Not because it feels right, but because the data says so.

individual.title: Data-informed exit decisions
individual.body: See how ready a student actually is for mainstream classes, and the deficits that are standing in their way.
individual.callout: What this means for you: tell a parent, a principal and a student exactly when they are ready to join mainstream, and why.
individual.readinessFooter: Aggregated from every subskill in all four domains.

cohort.title: Plan the program
cohort.body: See the whole cohort's readiness in one view and forecast next term's exits and intakes before you set the timetable.
cohort.callout: What this means for you: answer “how many are leaving us next term” with a number instead of an estimate.

predict.quote:
Teacher intuition plus SchoolTest empiricism.

That is the difference.

hero.title: Paste the profile into AI. <blue>Get a week of content out.</blue>
hero.body: Export a privacy-safe individual or class set and hand it to ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude. Real subskill data turns a generic prompt into personalised teaching content.

generate.title: From diagnostic profile to lesson materials in minutes.
generate.body: Personalised learning needs diagnostic data. Drop a student or class profile into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude and ask for a group reading passage with differentiated question sets. You'll have it before the kettle boils.
generate.callout: What this means for you: differentiation stops being a Sunday night job.
generate.promptText: “Write one passage at the class’s vocabulary band, with question sets matched to their gaps.”

classroom.title: Who to pair with whom, and how to split the room.
classroom.body: Each student and small group needs something slightly different. The diagnostic data makes your classroom management defensible, not just instinctive.
classroom.callout: What this means for you: let the data do the planning so you can do the teaching.

threeMore.title: And three more things it makes possible.
threeMore.groupByGapTitle: Group by gap, not by band
threeMore.groupByGapDescription: Split the room by shared weakness rather than overall level. Four groups, four genuinely different needs.
threeMore.pairBySkillTitle: Pair on the skill, not the level
threeMore.pairBySkillDescription: Two students both stuck on inference get further together. Or pair strong with struggling, skill by skill, so both have a reason to be there.
threeMore.parentUpdatesDescription: Turn a profile into plain language: what their child can do now, and what's next.

teach.note: No AI in your school? The subskill data still tells you who to pair and how to group. You just do the sorting yourself.
teach.quote:
A generic prompt gives you a worksheet.

Real data gives you a lesson.

hero.title: Progress you can measure, not just feel.
hero.body: Re-test any skill in 30 minutes, as often as your teaching cycle needs. Every result sits on the same scale, so you always know what moved and by how much.

evidence.title: Data-driven progress tracking
evidence.body: Once a week, once a month, whatever your teaching cycle needs. Growth maps to the ACARA continuum. The kind of data parents understand and a principal can act on.
evidence.callout: What this means for you: an evidence trail that works in parent meetings and in reports to leadership.
evidence.footer: ACARA EAL/D phases. Same scale every time.

teachEmpirical.title: Teach like a scientist.
teachEmpirical.body: Three weeks of targeted vocabulary work either shows up in the data or it doesn't. You find out sooner rather than later.
teachEmpirical.callout: What this means for you: feedback on your teaching, not just on your students.

cta.title: We're building this with founding schools.
cta.body: Field testing now. Early access, direct input into the reports, founding terms at launch.

shared.nextPredictDescription: Know when they're ready to exit.

footer.tagline: Diagnostic English assessment for Australian EAL/D classrooms. Years 7–12, ACARA phases and CEFR bands.

meta.title: Test-day run sheet - SchoolTest
meta.description: What to say and do before, during and after the sitting.

RunSheet.title: Test-day run sheet
RunSheet.subtitle: Everything you need to run the sitting, step by step. Print it out and keep it close by.

before.title: Before the day
before.itemOne: Check your class list ahead of time: every student needs their correct school email to log in. Fix any wrong emails before test day.
before.itemTwo: On the day, open the test-day screen for your class and start a sitting.

start.title: When you start
start.itemOne: Reveal the access code on the test-day screen and write it on the board.
start.itemTwo: Students open the SchoolTest app, enter the code and their school email, and begin.

say.title: What to tell your students
say.intro: Say this to the class before they begin:
say.lineTwo: Each part gets a bit harder, so do not worry if it feels that way.
say.lineThree: If you do not know an answer, have your best guess and move on.
say.lineFour: When the time runs out, the app moves you on by itself.
say.lineFive: Between the parts you can take a moment, and tap continue when you are ready.

during.title: During the test
during.itemOne: Walk the room and supervise as you normally would.
during.itemTwo: The class progress list on the test-day screen shows who has joined, who is working and who has submitted.
during.itemThree: You cannot pause or change the test, and you do not need to start the breaks. Each student taps continue when they are ready.

trouble.title: If something goes wrong
trouble.itemOne: A student who is away sits later. Keep the sitting open or start a new one when they are back, and reveal the code for them.
trouble.itemTwo: If the app crashes or a laptop goes flat, choose Re-sit next to the student's name on the test-day screen. The student joins again with the code and their school email.

after.title: After the test
after.itemOne: When every student has submitted, close the sitting on the test-day screen.
after.itemTwo: Results appear on your dashboard once the scoring has finished.
